Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the FCIC/RMA filing calendar and timeliness evidence; escalation to Head of Compliance

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 2026 SRA Section I (Agent / Agent of Record definitions), Section II(a)(2) Plan of Operations due date, Appendix III data reporting requirements and the RMA M13 transaction cutoff schedule, re-read each reinsurance year on SRA reissue

In-scope processes.value: Every recurring FCIC/RMA submission for the reinsurance year: weekly eDAS/PASS data transmissions by the transaction cutoff date, Appendix III monthly and annual reports, the April 1 Plan of Operations, and the per-agent state licensing evidence backing the agent-of-record roster reported to RMA

In-scope systems.value: Filing calendar mastered in the Internal Regulatory System; RMA eDAS/PASS acceptance reports attached per calendar row

Compliance procedure documented.value: FCIC Filing Calendar Procedure — annual SRA deadline harvest, calendar build, owner assignment, receipt capture within 1 business day of each submission, and the weekly transaction-cutoff checkpoint

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance; re-approved each reinsurance year within 30 days of RMA reissuing the SRA and its appendices

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Weekly transaction cutoff (per RMA M13 schedule), Appendix III monthly reports, Plan of Operations by April 1, and reports due within 45 days of an FCIC request — each a dated calendar row with an owner

Deadline reminders configured.value: Calendar alerts at T-14/T-7/T-2 days to every RMA due date, plus a standing Monday reminder for that week's transaction cutoff, routed to the owning analyst and the Regulatory Reporting Manager

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Submission confirmations, eDAS acceptance reports and dated agent licensing extracts retained for the SRA record period (reinsurance year plus 3 years, hold extended during any FCIC review) in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any missed or late RMA submission, eDAS rejection not cured by the next cutoff, or roster agent without licensing evidence is logged with root cause and disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Head of Compliance signs off closure of every late-filing or missing-evidence exception before the calendar row is marked cured

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All FCIC/RMA calendar rows due in the reinsurance year to date (weekly cutoffs, monthly Appendix III reports, Plan of Operations, FCIC-requested reports) plus the full agent-of-record roster reported to RMA

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on the Plan of Operations and annual submissions; ≤2% late weekly transmissions provided each was cured by the following cutoff; any agent row without dated state licensing evidence is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous; test runs quarterly over the quarter's calendar rows with 100% coverage of annual filings and a sample of weekly cutoffs

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have prepared or submitted any tested filing

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly filing-timeliness workpaper (calendar extract, receipt traces, NIPR re-checks, exceptions) filed in the compliance evidence repository under REG-056/C33

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Calendar export with per-row submission timestamps, eDAS acceptance reports and the agent licensing evidence index, producible to RMA within 5 business days of a request

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Reporting Manager fields RMA data inquiries; Regulatory Counsel clears any response admitting a late or missed submission before it goes to the RMA regional compliance office

checklist.step: Harvest every deadline from the new reinsurance year's SRA and appendices
actions: Download the reissued SRA, Appendix III and Appendix IV from the RMA website (rma.usda.gov ▸ Laws and Regulations ▸ Standard Reinsurance Agreement) when RMA posts them for the reinsurance year.

Read Section II(a)(2) and record the Plan of Operations due date (April 1 preceding the reinsurance year) and every dated obligation in Appendix III, including monthly and annual data reporting requirements.
Pull the RMA M13 data acceptance schedule and record the weekly transaction cutoff day and time for eDAS/PASS submissions.
List each harvested deadline on a worksheet with citation, due date, frequency and the artifact due.
checklist.done: a worksheet lists every SRA/Appendix III deadline for the reinsurance year with citation and due date.

checklist.step: Build the reinsurance-year filing calendar with one row per due submission
actions: In the Internal Regulatory System create one calendar row per submission instance: obligation name, SRA citation, due date, submission channel (eDAS/PASS, RMA regional office email, or RMA portal), owner and evidence type.
Expand recurring obligations into dated instances — 52 weekly transaction-cutoff rows, 12 monthly Appendix III rows, one April 1 Plan of Operations row.
Cross-check the row count against the harvest worksheet and have the Regulatory Reporting Manager initial the completeness check.
Lock prior-year rows so history cannot be edited.
checklist.done: the calendar carries a dated, owned row for every submission instance and the completeness check is initialed.

checklist.step: Configure reminders against every calendar row
actions: Set alerts at T-14, T-7 and T-2 days on every monthly and annual row, addressed to the row owner and the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
Set a standing Monday 09:00 reminder for the week's transaction cutoff naming the batch owner.
Route escalation of any row still open at T-1 to the Head of Compliance automatically.
Test-fire one reminder of each type and file the received copies as configuration evidence.
checklist.done: every row has T-14/T-7/T-2 alerts, the weekly cutoff reminder is live, and test-fire copies are filed.

checklist.step: Assign a preparer and a reviewer to each submission type
actions: Name a preparer and an independent reviewer for each obligation type on the calendar; the reviewer may not be the preparer.
Record backup owners so a vacancy never orphans a due date.
Publish the assignment matrix to the reporting team and file it with the calendar.
Re-confirm assignments within 5 business days whenever an owner leaves the team.
checklist.done: each obligation type has a named preparer, reviewer and backup recorded on the calendar.

checklist.step: Run the weekly eDAS/PASS transmission ahead of the transaction cutoff
actions: Extract the week's policy, acreage and claim transactions from the Policy Administration Platform in the RMA M13 record layouts.
Transmit the batch to RMA eDAS/PASS no later than the transaction cutoff date and time for the week.
Download the eDAS acceptance/rejection report the same day and hand rejected records to the data team for correction and retransmission before the next weekly cutoff.
Attach the transmission log and acceptance report to the week's calendar row and record the actual submission timestamp on the row.
checklist.done: the weekly batch was transmitted by the cutoff, the acceptance report is attached, and rejects are queued for the next cutoff.

checklist.step: Capture a submission receipt for every non-weekly filing within 1 business day
actions: On submitting a monthly Appendix III report, the Plan of Operations, or any FCIC-requested report, save the portal confirmation page or the sent email to the RMA addressee as a PDF.
Name the file <obligation>-<due date>-submitted-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf and attach it to the calendar row within 1 business day.
Record the actual submission date on the row so timeliness is computable without opening the attachment.
File the receipt in the compliance evidence repository under REG-056/C33/<reinsurance year>.
checklist.done: every completed row shows an actual submission date with a named receipt attached and filed.

checklist.step: Maintain the agent-of-record roster with state licensing evidence per agent
actions: Pull the agent-of-record roster reported to RMA from the agency/producer management system for the reinsurance year.

For each agent, run a NIPR Producer Database lookup for every state in which that agent sells or services eligible crop insurance contracts and confirm an active crop or property/casualty line of authority for the reinsurance year, per SRA Section I's Agent / Agent of Record definitions.
Save the dated NIPR PDB report per agent and link it to the roster row.
Flag any agent without an active license in a serviced state to the Producer Compliance Manager the same day and suspend new business assignment to that agent.
checklist.done: every roster agent has a dated NIPR evidence file covering each serviced state, and gaps are flagged and suspended.

checklist.step: Refresh licensing evidence on roster changes and license renewals
actions: On every agent add, transfer or termination in the agency/producer management system, re-run the NIPR check before the roster change is reported to RMA.
Re-verify all agents whose state licenses expire inside the reinsurance year within 10 business days after the expiry date.
Update the roster row with the new evidence file and the verification date.
Report roster changes to RMA through the next weekly eDAS transmission, no later than the transaction cutoff date for the week.
checklist.done: no roster change reaches RMA without a same-cycle NIPR re-verification on file.

checklist.step: Hold the weekly calendar checkpoint
actions: Every Monday review all calendar rows due in the next 14 days with the assigned preparers.
Confirm last week's transaction cutoff row is closed with its acceptance report attached; if not, open an exception immediately.
Reassign at-risk rows and record the reassignment on the row.
Minute the checkpoint in a running log filed with the calendar.
checklist.done: the checkpoint log shows the coming 14 days reviewed and last week's cutoff closed or excepted.

checklist.step: Submit the Plan of Operations by April 1
actions: Assemble the Plan of Operations per SRA Section II(a)(2) — projected premium by state and fund designation, financial statements and the supporting exhibits RMA prescribes.
Obtain CFO-delegate review of the financial exhibits and Head of Compliance review of the compliance representations before submission.
Submit to RMA through the prescribed channel no later than April 1 preceding the reinsurance year and capture the confirmation.
Attach the confirmation to the April 1 calendar row the same day.
checklist.done: the Plan of Operations was submitted on or before April 1 with the confirmation attached to its row.

checklist.step: Log every late, missed or rejected submission as an exception
actions: Raise a tracker issue the day a row goes past due, an eDAS batch rejection survives a second cutoff, or an agent evidence gap is found.
Record the obligation, due date, actual date, root cause (data late from source, owner vacancy, RMA system outage) and business impact.
Assign an owner and a remediation date; for repeated weekly-cutoff misses, add a corrective action to the procedure itself.
Notify the Head of Compliance the same day on any exception touching an annual filing.
checklist.done: every timeliness failure has a tracker issue with root cause, owner and remediation date.

checklist.step: Get remediation sign-off before closing any exception
actions: Review the completed remediation against the tracker issue — the late filing made, the reject cured, or the agent re-licensed or removed from the roster.
Decide whether the failure must be disclosed to RMA and route any disclosure draft through Regulatory Counsel.
Sign and date the issue; only then may the calendar row be marked cured.
Return inadequate remediations to the owner with a revised date.
checklist.done: no exception is closed without a dated Head of Compliance sign-off and a disclosure decision.

checklist.step: Reconcile the calendar to actual RMA submissions monthly
actions: Export the month's calendar rows to Excel and tick each against the receipt or eDAS acceptance report attached to it.
Compare the eDAS acceptance summaries to the Policy Administration Platform extract logs to prove no weekly batch was skipped.
Record any row marked complete without a receipt as an evidence defect and chase the receipt within 5 business days.
File the signed reconciliation in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: the month's reconciliation is signed with every row tied to a receipt or an open defect.

checklist.step: Report timeliness performance to compliance leadership quarterly
actions: Build the quarterly Power BI view: on-time rate by obligation type, late rows with age, open exceptions and eDAS reject-cure aging.
Present to the Head of Compliance and the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager with the remediation status of each open item.
Record decisions (procedure changes, staffing, disclosure to RMA) in the meeting minutes.
File the deck and minutes with the quarter's evidence.
checklist.done: the quarterly report is presented, minuted and filed with decisions assigned.

checklist.step: Retain the year's calendar and evidence for the SRA record period
actions: At reinsurance-year end, archive the locked calendar, all receipts, acceptance reports, agent licensing evidence and exception records under REG-056/C33/<year>.
Apply the SRA retention label (reinsurance year plus 3 years, hold extended during any FCIC review or dispute).
Verify the archive is retrievable by obligation, due date and agent name.
Record the archive completion on the final calendar row.
checklist.done: the year's records are archived, retention-labelled and retrievable by obligation and agent.

testing.step: Build the population of every submission due in the review period
actions: Export all calendar rows with due dates inside the quarter from the Internal Regulatory System, including weekly cutoff rows.
Independently rebuild the expected row set from the SRA, Appendix III and the M13 cutoff schedule — do not let the calendar define its own completeness.
List any obligation present in the SRA but absent from the calendar as an automatic exception.
testing.done: the population is rebuilt from source text and reconciled to the calendar, with omissions listed.

testing.step: Reconcile the weekly transmissions to the policy admin extract logs
actions: Match each weekly calendar row to a Policy Administration Platform extract log and an eDAS acceptance report for the same week.
Confirm the acceptance report timestamp is on or before the M13 transaction cutoff for that week.
Flag any week with an extract but no acceptance report, or an acceptance after cutoff, as an exception.
testing.done: every week traces extract → transmission → acceptance by cutoff, or is excepted.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of submissions and agents
actions: Take 100% of annual and monthly rows in the quarter plus 8 randomly selected weekly cutoff rows (seeded, reproducible).
Draw 25 agents at random from the agent-of-record roster reported to RMA, covering at least 5 states.
Record seed, population sizes and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers all annual/monthly rows plus 25 roster agents.

testing.step: Trace each sampled filing to its receipt and recompute timeliness
actions: Open the receipt attached to each sampled row in the compliance evidence repository and read the submission timestamp from the receipt itself, not the row.
Recompute days-to-deadline against the SRA due date, including the April 1 Plan of Operations date.
Treat a row marked complete with no receipt, or a receipt dated after the due date, as a fail.
testing.done: each sampled row has a receipt-based timeliness recomputation in the workpaper.

testing.step: Re-perform the NIPR licensing check for each sampled agent
actions: For each sampled agent, run a fresh NIPR Producer Database lookup for every state that agent services and read the license status and line of authority for the reinsurance year.
Compare to the evidence file on the roster row and to the roster as reported to RMA.
Treat a serviced state with no active license, or an evidence file older than the last roster change, as an exception.
Capture the NIPR result pages into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled agent has an independent NIPR re-check with captured results matched to the roster.

testing.step: Verify reminders and escalations actually fired
actions: For 5 sampled rows, inspect the alert log in the Internal Regulatory System for the T-14/T-7/T-2 sends and the Monday cutoff reminder.
For any row that went past due, confirm the T-1 escalation to the Head of Compliance was generated.
Flag configuration gaps even where the filing was ultimately on time.
testing.done: alert logs evidence the configured reminders and escalations for every inspected row.

testing.step: Test the exception log for completeness and cure
actions: Compare every late or missed row found in testing to the tracker — an untracked failure is itself a finding.
Check each logged exception carries root cause, owner, remediation date and the Head of Compliance closure sign-off.
Confirm rejected eDAS records were retransmitted by the following weekly cutoff by tracing the cure batch.
testing.done: every failure is logged, dispositioned and signed off, with reject cures traced to the next cutoff.

testing.step: Recompute the deadline maths on the annual filings
actions: Re-read the SRA due-date language for the Plan of Operations (April 1) and each Appendix III report tested, and recompute the due dates independently.
Confirm any 45-day windows triggered by an FCIC request were counted from the request date, not from the calendar entry.
Treat a calendar row carrying a wrong due date as an exception even if the filing beat the true date.
testing.done: all sampled due dates recompute correctly from the SRA text.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise one tracker issue per confirmed exception with obligation, due date, evidence gap and compliance impact under the SRA.
Assign root cause (calendar omission, receipt not captured, licensing lapse, reject not cured) and an owner.
Set remediation dates and mark any agent-licensing fail for assessment of disclosure to RMA with Regulatory Counsel.
Carry open items into next quarter's test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception is logged with root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the on-time rate against the thresholds (zero tolerance annual, ≤2% cured weekly) and state a conclusion: effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective.
Have the independent reviewer — who prepared none of the tested filings — sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Head of Compliance and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-056/C33.
Record the reporting date and the minute reference in the workpaper.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and reporting reference is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the Certificate of Authority verification gate for each state/line before crop business is written; escalation to Regulatory Counsel

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 2026 SRA Section I (Agent / Agent of Record definitions) and Section II eligibility conditions requiring the Company to be duly licensed in each state where eligible crop insurance contracts are sold and serviced, re-read on each SRA reissue and each planned market entry

In-scope processes.value: Market-entry gate for every new state, county-expansion or crop-program addition: MPCI written under the SRA and state-regulated crop-hail both require the writing company's Certificate of Authority to list the state and the property/allied lines authority before the first application is accepted

In-scope systems.value: CoA status tracked against the NAIC company record (CoCode); market-entry gate flag maintained in the underwriting configuration so unauthorized states cannot be quoted

Compliance procedure documented.value: Market Entry Authority Verification Procedure — CoA inspection, line-of-authority mapping for crop (property/allied lines), UCAA expansion filing path, RMA Plan of Operations state-list alignment, and the gate release

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and Regulatory Counsel; reviewed annually before the April 1 Plan of Operations submission

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per market entry — CoA verification must close before the state is added to the Plan of Operations (due April 1) and before the sales closing date for the first crop year written in that state

Deadline reminders configured.value: Market-entry tracker alerts at T-60/T-30/T-10 days to the target sales closing date for any state whose CoA or UCAA expansion is still open

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Certified CoA copies, state amendment approvals, UCAA expansion correspondence and the signed gate-release memo retained for the SRA record period (reinsurance year plus 3 years) in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any policy quoted or written in a state/line not on the CoA, or any Plan of Operations state without a verified CoA, is logged as an exception with disposition and any state DOI or RMA disclosure

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Regulatory Counsel signs off remediation of every unauthorized-writing exception, including the decision on state DOI self-report

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All states and counties with crop premium written in the reinsurance year per the policy admin state ledger, plus every market entry approved in the period

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — one policy effective in a state or line not covered by the CoA on its effective date is a fail and a reportable event

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per market entry; test runs annually before the Plan of Operations submission plus a per-entry re-check within 30 days after each new state's first policy is issued

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have performed any of the tested CoA verifications

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual CoA coverage test workpaper (state ledger extract, CoA traces, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under REG-056/C34

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Per-state CoA evidence pack (certified copy, verification date, verifier) mapped to written premium, producible to a state DOI or RMA within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Counsel leads any state DOI unauthorized-transaction inquiry; the Regulatory Reporting Manager aligns any RMA-facing correction to the Plan of Operations

checklist.step: Register the proposed market entry and open a verification file
actions: Take the market-entry request from the Head of Distribution or the Insurance Product Manager: state, crop programs (MPCI plans, crop-hail), writing company and target first crop year.
Open a verification case named <writing company>-<state>-<reinsurance year> in the workflow/case management tool.
Record the target sales closing date for the earliest crop to be written in that state — the gate must close before it.
Attach the business case and the requested county/crop list.
checklist.done: a dated verification case exists with state, company, programs and the controlling sales closing date.

checklist.step: Pull the current Certificate of Authority for the writing company
actions: Retrieve the latest certified CoA for the writing company from the corporate licensing file in the document management repository.
Confirm the certificate on file is the current amendment — check the amendment date against the state DOI's company-search record for the writing company's NAIC CoCode.
Where the filed copy is stale, order a certified copy from the state DOI and file it on receipt.
List the authorized lines exactly as the certificate words them.
checklist.done: the current certified CoA is on file with its authorized lines transcribed into the case.

checklist.step: Map crop insurance to the state's line-of-authority taxonomy
actions: Determine which authorized line the state treats as covering MPCI and crop-hail — typically property or allied lines (NAIC line 2.1 Allied Lines for crop-hail; MPCI reported on the state page as allied lines/federal crop).
Read the state insurance code's classification section and note the citation in the case.
Where the state requires a separate crop or hail authority, record that as the required line.
Write a one-paragraph opinion naming the required authority and cite it.
checklist.done: the case states the exact line of authority the state requires for the requested crop programs, with citation.

checklist.step: Verify the CoA covers the state and the required line before any writing
actions: Compare the transcribed CoA lines to the required line from counsel's mapping for the entry state.
Verify the certificate is active — no suspension, restriction or pending revocation — via the state DOI company search and the NAIC company record for the CoCode.
Record the verification result, date and verifier on the case: COVERED, NOT COVERED, or RESTRICTED.
For NOT COVERED or RESTRICTED, stop the entry and route to the UCAA expansion step — never write around a missing authority.
checklist.done: the case shows a dated COVERED/NOT COVERED determination against the required line, made before any policy is quoted.

checklist.step: File the UCAA expansion where authority is missing
actions: Prepare the NAIC UCAA Expansion Application (or the state's corporate amendment form) for the missing line or state: application form, certificate of compliance from the domestic state, financial statements and the filing fee per the state's UCAA chart.
Submit through the state's prescribed channel and record the submission date and fee paid.
Track the state's review, answer deficiency letters within the state's stated response window, and log each contact.
On approval, obtain the amended certified CoA and file it in the document management repository; update the case to COVERED.
checklist.done: the amended CoA listing the new state/line is on file and the case moved to COVERED, or the entry remains blocked.

checklist.step: Align the Plan of Operations state list with verified authorities
actions: Before the April 1 Plan of Operations submission to RMA, compare every state on the projected premium exhibit to a COVERED verification case.
Remove or footnote any state whose CoA verification or UCAA expansion is still open.
Attach the reconciliation to the Plan of Operations workpapers.
Notify the Head of Distribution of any state dropped from the plan and why.
checklist.done: every state in the Plan of Operations has a COVERED verification on file dated before April 1.

checklist.step: Release the market-entry gate in the underwriting configuration
actions: On written confirmation of COVERED status from the Producer Licensing Coordinator, enable the state and crop programs in the Underwriting Platform state-availability table.
Set the earliest-quote date no earlier than the verification date and no later than the sales closing date.
Leave every unverified state disabled so a quote in that state hard-stops.
Attach the configuration change record to the verification case.
checklist.done: the state is quotable only after COVERED confirmation, and the configuration change is evidenced on the case.

checklist.step: Confirm county and crop program availability with RMA before first sales
actions: In the RMA Actuarial Information Browser (webapp.rma.usda.gov/apps/actuarialinformationbrowser) look up the entry state's counties and confirm the intended MPCI plans and crops carry actuarial documents for the crop year.
Record the sales closing dates per crop/county from the actuarial documents into the case.
Hand the county/crop availability list to the Head of Distribution so marketing matches what can lawfully be written.
Flag any county where the crop program is unavailable so it is excluded from the launch.
checklist.done: the case holds the RMA county/crop availability list with sales closing dates matching the launch plan.

checklist.step: Monitor CoA status changes for all active crop states
actions: Maintain a state-by-state CoA register in the Internal Regulatory System: line authority, certificate date, last verification date, restrictions.
Re-verify each active crop state annually before the Plan of Operations and within 5 business days of any state DOI notice touching the certificate.
Subscribe to each active state DOI's bulletin list and route certificate-related notices to the register owner.
Escalate any suspension or restriction to Regulatory Counsel and the Chief Underwriting Officer the same day, with a stop-writing recommendation.
checklist.done: the register shows an annual re-verification per active state and same-day escalation on any adverse status change.

checklist.step: Handle renewals, redomestications and corporate changes that touch the CoA
actions: Track each state's CoA renewal/continuation requirement (annual continuation fees, corporate amendments on name, address, officers) on the register with due dates.
File corporate amendment notices within each state's window after any name change, merger or redomestication of the writing company.
Obtain and file the reissued certificates after every change.
Update the verification cases of affected states with the new certificate reference.
checklist.done: no state's CoA lapses for an unpaid continuation or unfiled corporate amendment, and reissued certificates are filed.

checklist.step: Block and unwind any business found written without authority
actions: On discovery of a policy in a state/line not on the CoA, open a tracker issue the same day and disable the state in the Underwriting Platform immediately.
Quantify the exposure with the UW Operations Manager: policy count, premium, effective dates, counties.
With Regulatory Counsel, determine the state's unauthorized-transaction consequences and whether a self-report to the state DOI and a disclosure to RMA are required.
Execute the counsel-approved remedy (obtain authority retroactively where the state permits, non-renew, or novate to an authorized affiliate) and document each policy's disposition.
checklist.done: the state is blocked, the exposure quantified, the counsel-decided remedy executed and each policy dispositioned.

checklist.step: Capture Regulatory Counsel sign-off on every remediation
actions: Review the completed remediation of each unauthorized-writing exception against the tracker issue.
Confirm the self-report decision was executed as decided and file the state DOI correspondence.
Sign and date the issue; only counsel's signature closes it.
Feed any procedure weakness back into the Market Entry Authority Verification Procedure within 30 days.
checklist.done: every exception closes on a dated counsel signature with the disclosure record filed.

checklist.step: Brief distribution before each new-state launch
actions: Before first sales in the entry state, brief the Agency Relations Manager and affected agencies on what is authorized: state, lines, plans, counties.
Distribute the do-not-write list of adjacent states still unverified.
Collect acknowledgment from each agency principal and file it on the case.
Repeat the briefing whenever the authorized scope changes.
checklist.done: agencies hold a written authorized-scope brief with filed acknowledgments before launch.

checklist.step: Reconcile written premium to authorized states quarterly
actions: Extract premium by state, line and writing company from the Policy Administration Platform for the quarter.
Compare every state with premium > 0 to the CoA register's COVERED list as of each policy's effective date.
Log any mismatch as an exception the same day and trigger the unwind step.
File the signed reconciliation in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: the quarterly reconciliation shows every premium-bearing state COVERED at effective date, or exceptions raised.

checklist.step: Retain the market-entry evidence pack
actions: Assemble per entry: verification case, certified CoA, counsel line mapping, UCAA correspondence, gate-release memo, configuration record and launch briefing acknowledgments.
File under REG-056/C34/<state>/<reinsurance year> with the SRA retention label (reinsurance year plus 3 years, extended during any review).
Verify retrievability by state, writing company and crop year.
Log the retention completion on the case before it closes.
checklist.done: each market entry has a complete, retention-labelled evidence pack retrievable by state and year.

testing.step: Build the population of states and entries with crop writings
actions: Extract from the Policy Administration Platform every state/writing-company pair with crop premium effective in the reinsurance year, with first-policy effective dates.
Add every market-entry case opened in the period from the workflow/case management tool, including blocked entries.
Reconcile the premium extract to the statutory state pages so no writing state is missed.
testing.done: a reconciled population of premium-bearing states and entry cases is documented.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the CoA register
actions: Match every premium-bearing state to a register row with status COVERED and a verification date before the state's first policy effective date.
List any state missing from the register, or verified after first writing, as an automatic exception.
Confirm blocked entries show no premium.
testing.done: every writing state matches a pre-dated COVERED register row or is excepted.

testing.step: Draw the sample
actions: Take 100% of market entries completed in the period plus 10 randomly selected continuing states (seeded, reproducible).
Include every state that had a DOI notice, restriction or corporate amendment during the period.
Record seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all new entries and 10 continuing states is drawn.

testing.step: Re-perform the CoA verification for each sampled state
actions: Pull the certified CoA from the document management repository and independently read the authorized lines and certificate date.
Check the writing company's current status on the sampled state DOI's company search and the NAIC company record for the CoCode.
Reach an independent COVERED/NOT COVERED conclusion before reading the case, then compare; any difference — including right answer from a stale certificate — is an exception.
Capture the certificate page and the DOI status screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled state has an independent re-verification with captured evidence and a comparison note.

testing.step: Re-perform the line-of-authority mapping
actions: For 5 sampled states, re-read the state insurance code classification cited in counsel's mapping.
Confirm the line held on the CoA genuinely covers MPCI and crop-hail as written in that state.
Flag any mapping resting on an uncited assumption as an exception.
testing.done: the sampled mappings re-derive to the same required line from the cited code sections.

testing.step: Trace the gate release to the underwriting configuration
actions: For each sampled entry, read the Underwriting Platform state-availability change record and its enable date.
Confirm the enable date is on or after the COVERED verification date and that no quote pre-dates it by inspecting the earliest quote log for the state.
Attempt a test quote in a still-unverified state in the test environment and confirm the hard stop fires.
testing.done: every sampled state was enabled only after verification, and the hard stop is proven to work.

testing.step: Recompute the deadline alignment for entries feeding the Plan of Operations
actions: For each sampled entry in the Plan of Operations, confirm the COVERED date precedes April 1 of the submission year.
Recompute the gap between the COVERED date and the state's first sales closing date and confirm the gate closed first.
Treat a plan state verified after April 1 as an exception even if no premium resulted.
testing.done: sampled plan states verify before April 1 and before their first sales closing date.

testing.step: Test the exception handling for any unauthorized writing
actions: For every exception in the period, read the tracker issue: same-day state block, exposure quantification, counsel decision on self-report, and policy-level disposition.
Trace the state DOI correspondence where a self-report was made.
Confirm closure carries the Regulatory Counsel signature and date.
testing.done: every unauthorized-writing exception shows block, quantification, counsel-decided disclosure and signed closure.

testing.step: Log test exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise one tracker issue per confirmed test exception with state, writing company, defect and regulatory impact.
Assign root cause (stale certificate, wrong line mapping, gate released early, register not updated) and an owner.
Set remediation dates and carry open items into the next annual test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: each test exception is logged with root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compare results to the zero-tolerance threshold and state a conclusion: effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective.
Have the independent reviewer — who performed none of the tested verifications — sign the workpaper.
Report to the Head of Compliance and the Chief Underwriting Officer and file the workpaper under REG-056/C34 in the compliance evidence repository.
Record the reporting date and minute reference.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to compliance and underwriting leadership.

checklist.step: Open an onboarding case for every prospective crop agent
actions: On referral from the Agency Relations Manager, create the agent record in the agency/producer management system with legal name, NPN, resident state and the states where the agent will sell and service crop contracts.
Set the record status to PENDING VERIFICATION so no solicitation material or portal access is issued.
Record the planned solicitation start date and the reinsurance year.
Attach the signed agency agreement referencing SRA Section I Agent / Agent of Record obligations.
checklist.done: each prospective agent has a PENDING record with NPN, state list and planned start date, and no access issued.

checklist.step: Verify the license in every sales and service state before solicitation
actions: Run a NIPR Producer Database report by NPN and read, for each state on the case: license status Active, license class, crop or property/casualty line of authority, and expiration date within the reinsurance year.
Save the dated PDB report to the agent record — this is the SRA Section I evidence of licensing for the agent of record.
Reject any state where the authority is missing or expired and remove it from the agent's permitted state list.
Only then flip the record to VERIFIED and release solicitation materials and Broker & Agent Portal credentials.
checklist.done: a dated NIPR PDB report covering every permitted state is on the record before status VERIFIED and any solicitation.

checklist.step: Re-verify immediately before appointment and submit the appointment
actions: Within 5 business days before submitting the appointment, re-run the NIPR PDB check for each appointment state — a verification older than that is stale for this purpose.
In NIPR Gateway submit the appointment for each state that requires carrier appointment for crop lines, and pay the state appointment fee.
Save the NIPR transaction confirmation with its tracking number to the agent record.
Record the appointment effective date; solicitation may continue but no application may be countersigned before it where the state requires appointment first.
checklist.done: each appointment state shows a fresh PDB re-check and a NIPR appointment confirmation with tracking number.

checklist.step: Report new and changed agents to RMA by the weekly cutoff
actions: Include every verified agent add, state change and termination in the week's eDAS/PASS transmission in the M13 agent record layout.
Transmit no later than the transaction cutoff date for the week and pull the acceptance report.
Correct any rejected agent records and retransmit by the next cutoff.
Confirm back to the Producer Licensing Coordinator that each roster change was accepted.
checklist.done: every roster change reached RMA by the weekly cutoff with an acceptance report on file.

checklist.step: Enroll each new loss adjuster in the Appendix IV training program
actions: On hire or contract of a new loss adjuster, create the training plan in the learning management system: at least 60 total hours on FCIC-approved policy and procedure, of which at least 24 are classroom.
Build the syllabus from the FCIC-18010 Crop Insurance Handbook, the LASH loss adjustment standards and the crop-specific loss adjustment handbooks for the crops the adjuster will handle.
Schedule the classroom sessions and record planned hours per module.
Set the adjuster's Claims Platform assignment eligibility to BLOCKED until the gate clears.
checklist.done: each new adjuster has a 60/24-hour plan built from FCIC-approved materials and a BLOCKED assignment status.

checklist.step: Deliver and evidence the 60 hours with classroom sign-ins
actions: Deliver the classroom modules and collect a signed attendance sheet per session with date, module, hours and instructor.
Record self-study and field-shadowing hours in the learning management system against the plan, with the supervising adjuster named for field hours.
Reconcile total recorded hours to the 60/24 requirement and chase shortfalls before the competency test is offered.
Upload sign-in sheets to the adjuster's training record.
checklist.done: the LMS transcript shows ≥60 total and ≥24 classroom hours, each backed by a sign-in sheet or a named supervisor.

checklist.step: Administer and grade the basic competency test
actions: Administer the written competency test covering FCIC-approved policy and procedure — claim standards under 7 CFR 457.8 section 14, LASH procedures, appraisal methods and documentation requirements.
Grade against the published pass mark and record the score, date and version of the test in the learning management system.
For failures, prescribe remedial modules and a retest date; the assignment block stays on.
File the graded test paper in the adjuster's record as an FCIC-reviewable document.
checklist.done: a graded, dated test with score and version is on each adjuster's record, passed before any assignment.

checklist.step: Release the claim-assignment gate only on a complete record
actions: Check the adjuster's record shows: 60/24 hours evidenced, competency test passed, and any state adjuster license the work state requires verified.
Flip the Claims Platform eligibility from BLOCKED to ELIGIBLE with the release date and releaser recorded.
Restrict the crops the adjuster may handle to those covered by the completed crop-specific modules.
Confirm the assignment engine cannot route claims to BLOCKED adjusters by checking the routing rule.
checklist.done: no adjuster becomes ELIGIBLE without the evidenced 60/24 hours, a passed test and required state licenses.

checklist.step: Run the annual refresher and proficiency requirements for experienced adjusters
actions: Assign the annual update training covering crop-year procedure changes from RMA bulletins and reissued handbooks before the crop year's first loss notices.
Track completion in the learning management system and re-block any adjuster who misses the deadline.
Record annual performance evaluations per Appendix IV, including field reviews by the quality function.
File the annual rosters as FCIC-reviewable records.
checklist.done: every active adjuster completed the crop-year refresher before first losses, or was re-blocked.

checklist.step: Monitor for mid-year license lapses and disciplinary actions
actions: Subscribe the agent roster to NIPR PDB alerts (or re-run monthly PDB batch checks) for status changes, expirations and regulatory actions.
On a lapse or action, set the agent's record to SUSPENDED the same day and notify the Agency Relations Manager and the affected agency in writing.
Hold all pending applications from that agent until the license is restored and re-verified.
Log the event and its resolution on the agent record.
checklist.done: lapses and actions surface within the monthly cycle, trigger same-day suspension, and are logged with resolution.

checklist.step: Gate application intake on the soliciting agent's verified status
actions: Configure the Underwriting Platform intake to require an agent-of-record code with status VERIFIED for the application's state before an application can be accepted.
Hard-stop applications carrying a SUSPENDED or unknown agent code and route them to the Producer Licensing Coordinator.
Review the hard-stop log weekly with the Producer Compliance Manager.
Evidence the configuration and each weekly review.
checklist.done: intake rejects applications from unverified agents and the hard-stop log is reviewed weekly.

checklist.step: Log and remediate every gate breach
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any solicitation before verification, countersignature before required appointment, or claim adjusted by a BLOCKED adjuster.
For adjuster breaches, commission a re-review of the affected claims by an eligible adjuster and record corrected findings.
Assign root cause (verification skipped, stale PDB, routing rule failure) and remediation owner.
Obtain the Chief Claims Officer counter-signature on adjuster-gate breaches before closure.
checklist.done: each breach has a tracker issue, affected claims re-reviewed, root cause assigned and required signatures captured.

checklist.step: Reconcile rosters across systems monthly
actions: Export the agent roster from the agency/producer management system, the RMA-reported roster from the weekly transmissions, and the adjuster eligibility list from the Claims Platform.
Three-way match in Excel: every RMA-reported agent VERIFIED, every ELIGIBLE adjuster gate-complete, no orphans in any list.
Raise mismatches as exceptions the same day.
File the signed reconciliation in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: the monthly three-way reconciliation is signed with all mismatches raised as exceptions.

checklist.step: Brief agencies each reinsurance year on licensing obligations
actions: Before the reinsurance year's first sales closing date, issue the licensing bulletin to all agencies: verification before solicitation, state list discipline, renewal responsibilities.
Collect an acknowledgment from each agency principal.
Train the Agency Relations Manager team on the escalation path for licensing questions.
File the bulletin and acknowledgments.
checklist.done: the annual bulletin is issued with acknowledgments filed before the first sales closing date.

checklist.step: Retain licensing and training records for FCIC review
actions: File per agent: PDB reports, appointment confirmations and event log; per adjuster: training plan, transcripts, sign-in sheets, graded tests and annual evaluations.
Index under REG-056/C35 by name, NPN and reinsurance year with the SRA retention label.
Verify sampled records retrieve completely, since these are explicitly subject to FCIC review.
Log retention completion quarterly.
checklist.done: agent and adjuster records are indexed, retention-labelled and retrievable for FCIC review.

testing.step: Build the population of new agents and newly eligible adjusters
actions: Extract all agent records created or state-expanded in the period from the agency/producer management system with their VERIFIED dates.
Extract all adjusters whose Claims Platform status moved to ELIGIBLE in the period with release dates and first assignment dates.
Reconcile the agent extract to the RMA-reported roster from the weekly transmissions and resolve differences before sampling.
testing.done: both populations are extracted with gate dates and reconciled to the RMA roster.

testing.step: Reconcile solicitations and assignments to gate dates
actions: Match each agent's earliest application in the Underwriting Platform intake log to the record's VERIFIED date; earlier solicitation evidence (portal first-login, first quote) counts too.
Match each adjuster's first Claims Platform assignment to the ELIGIBLE release date.
List every activity pre-dating its gate as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every first activity post-dates its gate or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw documented samples
actions: Sample 30 agents (seeded random, minimum 5 states represented) and 100% of new adjusters up to 20, random 20 beyond that.
Include every agent flagged SUSPENDED during the period.
Record seed, population sizes and selection date.
testing.done: reproducible samples of agents and adjusters are drawn and recorded.

testing.step: Re-perform the NIPR verification for sampled agents
actions: Run a fresh NIPR PDB report per sampled agent and compare license status, lines and states to the PDB report saved at verification time.
Check the saved report's date precedes the VERIFIED status flip and the first solicitation.
Check the pre-appointment re-check was within 5 business days of the NIPR appointment submission and trace the appointment confirmation tracking number.
Capture PDB result pages into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled agent shows a pre-solicitation PDB, a fresh pre-appointment re-check and a traced appointment confirmation.

testing.step: Trace sampled adjusters' 60/24 hours to primary evidence
actions: Open each sampled adjuster's LMS transcript and foot the hours: total ≥60, classroom ≥24.
Trace classroom hours to signed attendance sheets and field hours to the named supervising adjuster.
Confirm the syllabus modules map to FCIC-approved materials (FCIC-18010, LASH, crop handbooks) for the crops the adjuster handles.
Treat unevidenced hours as not completed.
testing.done: sampled transcripts foot to ≥60/≥24 with every hour traced to a sign-in sheet or named supervisor.

testing.step: Re-check the competency test evidence
actions: Inspect each sampled adjuster's graded test: score at or above the pass mark, date before the ELIGIBLE release, test version current for the crop year.
For any failure-then-retest, confirm remedial modules were completed between attempts.
Confirm the graded paper is filed in the compliance evidence repository as an FCIC-reviewable record.
testing.done: every sampled adjuster passed a current-version test before release, with retest remediation evidenced.

testing.step: Test the intake and assignment hard stops
actions: In the test environment, attempt to route a claim to a BLOCKED adjuster and submit an application under a SUSPENDED agent code; confirm both hard-stop.
Inspect the production hard-stop logs for the period and verify each stop was dispositioned by the Producer Licensing Coordinator.
Flag any override without a documented reason.
testing.done: both hard stops fire in test, and production stops are fully dispositioned.

testing.step: Recompute the weekly-cutoff timeliness of roster reporting
actions: For 10 sampled roster changes, compare the change date in the agency/producer management system to the eDAS transmission week that carried it.
Confirm each change went no later than the transaction cutoff date for its week, and rejects were retransmitted by the next cutoff.
Treat a change held past its week's cutoff as an exception.
testing.done: sampled roster changes each reached RMA by their week's cutoff or are excepted.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with agent/adjuster, defect, and the SRA/Appendix IV impact.
Assign root cause (gate skipped, stale verification, unevidenced hours, routing failure) and an owner with a remediation date.
For any claim adjusted by an unqualified adjuster, confirm the claim re-review is commissioned and note the FCIC-disclosure assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
Carry open items to the next semi-annual test.
testing.done: every exception is logged with root cause, owner, claim re-review where due, and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the conclusion against the zero-tolerance threshold: effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective.
Have the independent reviewer — who onboarded and trained none of the sampled individuals — sign the workpaper.
Report to the Producer Compliance Manager, the Chief Claims Officer and the Head of Compliance; file under REG-056/C35.
Record the reporting date and minute reference.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to licensing and claims leadership.

checklist.step: Maintain the per-state appointment and termination window matrix
actions: For every state where crop agents are appointed, record in the Internal Regulatory System: whether pre-appointment is required, the appointment window from first application (commonly 15 days), the termination-notice window (commonly 30 days), the producer-copy window (commonly 15 days), the annual renewal date and fee.
Cite each window to the state statute or regulation and attach the source extract.
Have Regulatory Counsel validate the matrix annually and on any state bulletin changing a window.
Version the matrix so the window in force at any event date is provable.
checklist.done: a counsel-validated, versioned matrix carries cited windows and renewal dates for every appointment state.

checklist.step: Capture every triggering event with its clock-start date
actions: Log each event in the agency/producer management system queue: new agency agreement signed, first application received from an unappointed agent, resignation letter, agency decision to terminate, or discovery of cause.
Record the clock-start date the statute uses — first application date for appointments, termination effective date for notices — not the date the paperwork reached the team.
Compute and store the statutory due date from the matrix version in force.
Attach the trigger document (application header, resignation letter, termination memo).
checklist.done: every event carries a trigger document, the statutory clock-start date and a computed due date.

checklist.step: Submit appointments in NIPR Gateway inside the state window
actions: In NIPR Gateway open Appointments ▸ New Appointment, select the writing company, the state and the agent's NPN, and choose the line the state uses for crop business.
Submit before the computed due date and pay the state appointment fee through Gateway.
Download the transaction confirmation with its NIPR tracking number and attach it to the event.
Where the state requires appointment before solicitation, confirm with the UW Operations Manager that intake was blocked until this confirmation.
checklist.done: the appointment shows a NIPR confirmation dated inside the window with the fee paid and attached.

checklist.step: Process ordinary terminations inside the notice window
actions: In NIPR Gateway open Appointments ▸ Termination, select the agent and state, enter the termination effective date and the reason code for a not-for-cause termination.
Submit within the state's notice window (30 days typical) from the termination effective date.
Send the producer their copy of the termination notice within the producer-copy window (15 days typical) by a trackable method and file the proof of sending.
Set the agent's record to TERMINATED so no further applications route under that code.
checklist.done: state notice and producer copy both went inside their windows with confirmations filed, and the code is closed.

checklist.step: Escalate for-cause terminations to counsel before filing
actions: Review every termination where cause is alleged — misappropriation, forgery, misrepresentation on applications, licensing fraud — before the NIPR transaction is submitted.
Settle the exact statutory disclosure wording for the state's for-cause reporting requirement and any accompanying documentation duty.
Confirm the producer-notification copy and the producer's statutory right to respond are honored.
Record the counsel review date on the event; the window clock does not pause for review, so complete it within 10 business days of discovery.
checklist.done: every for-cause termination carries a counsel-approved disclosure filed inside the statutory window.

checklist.step: Run the annual appointment renewal cycle per state
actions: At T-45 before each state's renewal date (several crop states invoice around April 1), pull the state's appointment invoice or run Appointment Renewal in NIPR Gateway for the writing company.
Reconcile the state's invoice list to the active roster — dispute ghosts and add omissions before paying.
Pay renewal fees by the state's date and file the receipt.
Terminate rather than renew agents inactive for the coming reinsurance year, feeding the termination step.
checklist.done: every state's renewal is reconciled, paid by its date, and inactive agents are terminated instead of renewed.

checklist.step: Synchronize every event to the RMA roster by the weekly cutoff
actions: Include each appointment and termination in the week's eDAS/PASS agent record transmission, no later than the transaction cutoff date for the week.
Pull the acceptance report and correct rejects by the next cutoff.
For terminated agents of record, coordinate with the UW Operations Manager on transferring the book so policyholder service continues per SRA Section IV(d).
Confirm synchronization back on the event record.
checklist.done: every event reached the RMA roster by its week's cutoff and books of terminated agents are reassigned.

checklist.step: Work the daily past-due digest to zero
actions: Open the daily digest of events at 50%/80% of window and past due from the agency/producer management system queue.
Action every 80% item the same day; log the blocking reason where an item cannot complete (state portal outage, missing NPN).
Raise a tracker exception for anything that passes its due date, without waiting for month-end.
Hand persistent blockers to the Producer Compliance Manager within 2 business days.
checklist.done: the digest is worked daily, 80% items actioned same day, and past-due items are excepted immediately.

checklist.step: Verify fees and transactions cleared with the states
actions: Monthly, export NIPR Gateway transaction and fee reports and reconcile in Excel against the event queue: one confirmation per event, no unpaid fees, no rejected transactions left unworked.
Verify a sample of appointments against the state DOI's public appointment lookup to confirm the state actually recorded them.
Chase any NIPR transaction stuck in pending beyond 5 business days with the NIPR help desk and log the ticket.
File the signed reconciliation.
checklist.done: the monthly reconciliation ties every event to a cleared state transaction with no unworked rejects.

checklist.step: Keep producer notification proofs complete
actions: File the proof of sending (certified mail receipt, courier tracking, or e-delivery confirmation) for every producer termination copy in the document management repository against the event.
Record the sent date and verify it is inside the producer-copy window.
Where a producer disputes a for-cause characterization, route the response to Regulatory Counsel and file the correspondence with the event.
Flag any event missing its proof within 5 business days of the send date.
checklist.done: every termination event holds a dated proof of producer notification inside its window.

checklist.step: Log window breaches with disposition
actions: Raise a tracker issue the day any event passes its statutory due date unprocessed, with state, agent, event type, days late and root cause.
For late for-cause disclosures, notify Regulatory Counsel the same day for a state-notification decision.
Record the cure date and the late-filing consequence (state late fee, DOI inquiry) on the issue.
Trend root causes monthly and feed fixes into the procedure.
checklist.done: every breach is logged same-day with root cause, cure date and consequence recorded.

checklist.step: Obtain remediation sign-off
actions: Review each breach's cure — the late transaction completed, fees settled, disclosures made.
Obtain the Regulatory Counsel counter-signature on any for-cause defect.
Sign and date the issue; only then does it close.
Order a procedure or staffing change where the same root cause appears three times in a quarter.
checklist.done: no breach closes without the required signatures and a recurrence check.

checklist.step: Report window performance quarterly
actions: Build the quarterly view: on-window rate by state and event type, aging of open events, breach count and cure times.
Present to the Producer Compliance Manager and the Head of Compliance.
Minute decisions and file the deck with the quarter's evidence.
Feed states with recurring late events into the annual matrix revalidation.
checklist.done: the quarterly report is presented, minuted and filed with follow-ups assigned.

checklist.step: Align terminations with the agent-of-record transfer duty
actions: On every termination, reassign the agent's in-force crop policies to a licensed, appointed successor agent in the Policy Administration Platform before the next policy transaction (acreage report, claim, renewal).
Verify the successor's VERIFIED status with the Producer Licensing Coordinator before reassignment.
Notify affected policyholders of the servicing change where state law requires.
Record the transfer completion on the termination event.
checklist.done: every terminated agent's book is reassigned to a verified successor with the transfer recorded.

checklist.step: Retain the event evidence chain
actions: Archive per event: trigger document, window computation, NIPR confirmation, fee receipt, counsel review (for cause), producer proof and RMA synchronization note.
Index under REG-056/C36 by state, agent NPN and reinsurance year with the SRA-plus-state retention label.
Test retrieval quarterly on a sampled event.
Log retention completion.
checklist.done: each event's chain is archived, indexed and retrievable by state and NPN.

testing.step: Build the event population
actions: Extract all appointment, renewal and termination events for the quarter from the agency/producer management system event log with trigger dates and completion dates.
Independently pull the NIPR Gateway transaction report for the same period and reconcile counts both ways — an NIPR transaction without a queue event is as much a finding as the reverse.
Resolve differences before sampling.
testing.done: the event population reconciles two-way with the NIPR transaction report.

testing.step: Reconcile events to the RMA roster transmissions
actions: Match each completed event to the eDAS weekly transmission that carried it and read the acceptance report.
Confirm the carrying week's cutoff is on or after the event completion and no event waited more than one weekly cycle.
List unsynchronized events as exceptions.
testing.done: every event traces to an accepted RMA transmission within one weekly cycle.

testing.step: Draw the sample
actions: Take 100% of for-cause terminations, all breaches already logged, plus 30 seeded-random ordinary events covering at least 8 states and all three event types.
Verify the sample includes at least one annual-renewal state with an April 1 date where the period covers it.
Record seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: a reproducible sample with full for-cause coverage is drawn.

testing.step: Recompute every sampled window from statute
actions: For each sampled event, re-read the state's cited statute in the matrix version in force at the event date and independently recompute the due date from the trigger date.
Verify the queue's clock-start matches the statutory trigger (first application date, termination effective date) and not the paperwork arrival date.
Treat a wrong clock-start or wrong window as an exception even where the filing was early.
testing.done: all sampled due dates recompute correctly from statute and trigger evidence.

testing.step: Trace sampled events to NIPR confirmations
actions: Open the NIPR confirmation attached to each sampled event and read the transaction date, state, NPN and tracking number from the confirmation itself.
Confirm the transaction date is on or before the recomputed due date.
For 5 appointments, verify the appointment appears on the state DOI's public lookup.
Capture confirmations and lookup results into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled event has a confirmation dated inside its window, with state-side verification for 5.

testing.step: Test the for-cause disclosures end to end
actions: For each for-cause termination, verify the counsel review pre-dates the NIPR submission and the disclosure wording matches the counsel-approved text.
Confirm the producer copy went by a trackable method inside the producer-copy window and any producer response was filed and answered.
Confirm the reason code transmitted to the state matches the underlying cause file.
testing.done: every for-cause termination shows counsel review, timely disclosure, timely producer copy and a consistent reason code.

testing.step: Verify the renewal cycle for the period's renewal states
actions: For each state with a renewal date in the period, trace the invoice reconciliation, the payment receipt and the payment date against the state deadline (including April 1 states).
Confirm agents dropped at renewal generated termination events rather than silent lapses.
Treat an unreconciled invoice paid blind as an exception.
testing.done: each renewal state shows a reconciled, on-time payment and clean handling of dropped agents.

testing.step: Inspect the queue discipline and alerts
actions: Sample 5 days' past-due digests and verify same-day actioning of 80% items and immediate exceptions on past-due items.
Inspect the alert configuration for the 50%/80% window thresholds.
Flag any past-due event discovered in testing that never hit the tracker.
testing.done: digest discipline and alert configuration are evidenced, with untracked breaches flagged.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise one tracker issue per confirmed exception with state, event, days late and statutory citation.
Assign root cause (wrong clock-start, matrix stale, fee failure, counsel delay) and an owner with a remediation date.
Route late for-cause disclosures to Regulatory Counsel for the state-notification decision.
Carry open items to next quarter's test.
testing.done: every exception is logged with root cause, owner, counsel routing where due and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the on-window rate against the ≥98% threshold and the zero-tolerance items and state a conclusion: effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective.
Have the independent reviewer — who processed none of the sampled events — sign the workpaper.
Report to the Producer Compliance Manager and the Head of Compliance; file under REG-056/C36 in the compliance evidence repository.
Record the reporting date and minute reference.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and threshold comparison is filed and reported.
