checklist.step: Load every agent-state expiration into the renewal log
actions: Run a NIPR PDB batch report across the full crop agent roster and read each state license's expiration date and CE status flag.
Load one renewal-log row per agent per state in the agency/producer management system: NPN, state, line, expiration date, CE compliance date, agency.
Note each state's renewal scheme (birth month, fixed date, biennial anniversary) so clustered workload is visible in advance.
Refresh the batch quarterly and after every roster change.
checklist.done: the log holds one dated row per agent-state license, refreshed quarterly from NIPR PDB.

checklist.step: Configure the T-90/T-60/T-30 outreach ladder
actions: Set automatic reminders on every log row at T-90, T-60 and T-30 before expiration, addressed to the agent and copied to the agency principal.
Include in each notice the state, license number, expiration date, the state's CE requirement and the renewal path (NIPR Gateway or state portal).
Set the T-14 escalation to route to the Agency Relations Manager for direct follow-up.
Test-fire each rung and file the received copies.
checklist.done: every row carries the three-rung ladder plus T-14 escalation, with test-fires filed.

checklist.step: Check CE status before the renewal window
actions: At T-60, run a PDB check per expiring agent and read the CE compliance indicator for the renewal state.
For agents showing CE-deficient, request the outstanding hour count from the agent's state CE transcript (state portal or CE vendor) and record it on the row.
Notify the agent and agency in writing that renewal will be blocked by the state until CE completes, naming the hours outstanding.
Track the deficiency to closure before the expiration date.
checklist.done: every T-60 row shows a CE status, and each deficiency has a written notice and a tracked closure.

checklist.step: Confirm each renewal and re-verify the license
actions: Within 10 business days after each expiration date, run a NIPR PDB re-verification and read the new expiration date proving renewal.
Attach the dated PDB report to the log row and mark it RENEWED — this refreshed report is the SRA Section I licensing evidence for the rest of the reinsurance year.
Chase any row still showing the old date as an imminent lapse the same day.
Update the agent's permitted state list where a state was dropped at renewal.
checklist.done: every expiration resolves to a dated PDB re-verification showing the new term or an active lapse case.

checklist.step: Suspend on lapse the day it is confirmed
actions: Set the agent's record to SUSPENDED for the lapsed state the day the post-expiration PDB check confirms no renewal.
Verify the Underwriting Platform intake hard stop now rejects applications under that agent code for the lapsed state.
Notify the agent, the agency principal and the Agency Relations Manager in writing the same day, stating the reinstatement path.
Open a tracker issue to capture any business dated inside the lapse window.
checklist.done: confirmed lapses trigger same-day suspension, intake blocking, written notice and a tracker issue.

checklist.step: Sweep for business transacted during the lapse window
actions: Query the Policy Administration Platform for applications, acreage reports and endorsements carrying the lapsed agent's code with dates between expiration and reinstatement.
List each hit with policyholder, county, crop and transaction date on the tracker issue.
With Regulatory Counsel, determine the state-law consequence and whether the transaction needs re-execution by a licensed agent or disclosure.
Correct the agent of record on affected policies and re-transmit to RMA by the next weekly cutoff.
checklist.done: every lapse has a completed transaction sweep with counsel-decided handling and RMA corrections transmitted.

checklist.step: Verify reinstatement before lifting a suspension
actions: Require a fresh PDB report showing Active status and a current expiration before flipping SUSPENDED back to VERIFIED.
Confirm the state did not impose conditions (late renewal penalties, retest, new appointment) — where it did, evidence their satisfaction.
Where the state voided the appointment at lapse, resubmit the appointment in NIPR Gateway and attach the new confirmation.
Record the reinstatement date and evidence on the log row.
checklist.done: no suspension lifts without a fresh Active PDB report and any state conditions evidenced as satisfied.

checklist.step: Track the adjuster crop-year refresher to 100% before claim season
actions: Assign the annual refresher in the learning management system covering the crop year's procedure changes from RMA bulletins, reissued LASH standards and crop handbook updates.
Set the completion deadline ahead of the region's first expected loss notices and track completion weekly.
Re-block assignment eligibility in the Claims Platform for any adjuster past the deadline.
File the completion roster as an FCIC-reviewable record.
checklist.done: the refresher roster shows 100% completion before first losses, with laggards re-blocked.

checklist.step: Track state adjuster license renewals where the work state licenses adjusters
actions: Maintain renewal-log rows for adjuster licenses in states that license crop adjusters, with the same T-90/T-60/T-30 ladder.
Verify renewals through the state's adjuster lookup and attach dated evidence.
Coordinate with the Claims Director / Manager to re-block any adjuster whose state license lapses.
Record reciprocal-license dependencies where a home-state lapse cascades.
checklist.done: adjuster-license rows carry the same ladder and dated renewal evidence, with lapses re-blocking assignment.

checklist.step: Reconcile the renewal log to the live roster monthly
actions: Export the renewal log and the active roster and match in Excel: every active agent-state pair has a log row, and no log row survives for a terminated agent.
Verify every row that passed its expiration in the month shows RENEWED, SUSPENDED or an open lapse case — never blank.
Raise gaps as exceptions the same day.
File the signed reconciliation.
checklist.done: the monthly reconciliation proves full log coverage with no silently expired rows.

checklist.step: Report renewal and CE performance quarterly
actions: Build the quarterly view: renewal-before-expiry rate, lapse count and durations, CE deficiencies open, refresher completion, and business-in-lapse findings.
Present to the Producer Compliance Manager and the Head of Compliance with remediation status.
Minute decisions and file the deck.
Feed chronic-lapse agencies to the Agency Relations Manager for contract review.
checklist.done: the quarterly report is presented, minuted and filed with agency follow-ups assigned.

checklist.step: Log every lapse and refresher breach with disposition
actions: Raise one tracker issue per lapse and per refresher deadline miss with agent/adjuster, state, dates and days exposed.
Assign root cause (outreach ignored, CE shortfall, state processing delay, log gap) and an owner.
Record the disposition: reinstated, terminated, book transferred, claims re-reviewed.
Trend root causes quarterly.
checklist.done: every lapse and refresher miss has a tracker issue with root cause, owner and disposition.

checklist.step: Obtain remediation sign-off
actions: Review each closed lapse: sweep completed, counsel decision executed, RMA roster corrected, reinstatement evidenced.
Sign and date the issue; only then does it close.
Order termination proceedings for agents with repeat lapses in consecutive cycles.
Confirm any FCIC-facing correction was transmitted.
checklist.done: no lapse issue closes without a signed review confirming sweep, correction and reinstatement evidence.

checklist.step: Revalidate state CE and renewal rules annually
actions: Once per reinsurance year, re-read each serviced state's renewal statute and CE rule and update the state-rules table in the Internal Regulatory System (hours, ethics hours, exemptions, renewal scheme).
Cite each rule and attach the source extract.
Diff against the prior year and push changes into the renewal log logic and the outreach templates.
Have Regulatory Counsel validate the diff.
checklist.done: the state-rules table is re-cited annually with counsel-validated changes propagated to the log.

checklist.step: Retain the cycle's evidence
actions: Archive the year's renewal log versions, outreach copies, PDB re-verifications, lapse cases and refresher rosters under REG-056/C37/<reinsurance year>.
Apply the SRA retention label (reinsurance year plus 3 years, extended during any review).
Verify retrievability by agent NPN, state and expiration date.
Log retention completion.
checklist.done: the cycle's records are archived, retention-labelled and retrievable by NPN and state.

testing.step: Build the population of expirations and refresher obligations
actions: Extract every renewal-log row with an expiration date in the period, plus the adjuster refresher roster with its deadline.
Independently run a NIPR PDB batch over the active roster and rebuild the expected expiration set — the log must not define its own completeness.
List any active agent-state license absent from the log as an automatic exception.
testing.done: the expiration population is rebuilt from PDB and reconciled to the log with omissions listed.

testing.step: Reconcile lapse flags to intake and assignment blocks
actions: For every SUSPENDED period in the quarter, confirm the Underwriting Platform hard stop was active for the agent-state from the suspension date.
Confirm re-blocked adjusters had no Claims Platform assignments during their block.
Flag any window where the flag and the block disagree.
testing.done: every suspension traces to an active block with no assignment or intake leakage.

testing.step: Draw the sample
actions: Take 100% of lapses and refresher misses, plus 30 seeded-random renewed rows across at least 8 states and both fixed-date and birth-month schemes.
Include 10 adjusters from the refresher roster.
Record seed, population sizes and selection date.
testing.done: a reproducible sample with full lapse coverage is drawn.

testing.step: Re-perform the renewal verification on sampled rows
actions: Run a fresh NIPR PDB report per sampled agent-state and read the current expiration date.
Compare to the PDB report attached at RENEWED time and confirm that report post-dates the old expiration by no more than 10 business days.
Treat a RENEWED row whose evidence is a pre-expiration report as unproven.
Capture result pages into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled RENEWED row is re-proven by a fresh PDB read with correctly dated evidence.

testing.step: Recompute the outreach ladder dates
actions: For 10 sampled rows, recompute T-90/T-60/T-30 from the expiration date and match to the sent notices in the log.
Verify the T-14 escalation fired for rows still unrenewed at that point.
Treat a missing rung as an exception even where the agent renewed on time.
testing.done: sampled rows show correctly dated ladder sends and escalations.

testing.step: Re-perform the lapse sweeps
actions: For each lapse, independently re-run the transaction query for the lapse window in the Policy Administration Platform.
Compare hits to the sweep on the tracker issue — an unswept transaction is a fail.
Verify counsel's handling decision was executed per transaction and the RMA correction went by the next weekly cutoff.
Confirm reinstatement evidence includes any state-imposed conditions.
testing.done: independent sweeps match the recorded sweeps and every hit shows executed handling and RMA correction.

testing.step: Verify CE deficiency handling
actions: For sampled rows flagged CE-deficient at T-60, trace the written notice, the tracked hour count and the closure before expiration.
For rows that lapsed on CE grounds, confirm the deficiency was flagged at T-60 and not discovered post-expiry.
Flag any CE deficiency first surfacing after the expiration date as a monitoring failure.
testing.done: CE deficiencies trace from T-60 flag through notice to closure or a properly handled lapse.

testing.step: Verify the refresher gate held for claim season
actions: For the 10 sampled adjusters, read LMS completion dates against the refresher deadline and the region's first loss-notice date.
Confirm any adjuster completing late had no claim assignments between deadline and completion.
Trace the completion roster filed as the FCIC-reviewable record.
testing.done: sampled adjusters completed before first losses or were provably assignment-blocked until completion.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise one tracker issue per confirmed exception with agent/adjuster, state, defect and exposure window.
Assign root cause (log omission, evidence mis-dated, sweep incomplete, block leakage) and an owner with a remediation date.
Route any business-in-lapse finding to Regulatory Counsel for the disclosure decision.
Carry open items to the next semi-annual test.
testing.done: every exception is logged with root cause, owner, counsel routing where due and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the renew-before-expiry rate against ≥98%, the zero-tolerance lapse-business check and the 100% refresher check, and state a conclusion: effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective.
Have the independent reviewer — who maintains no part of the renewal log — sign the workpaper.
Report to the Producer Compliance Manager and the Head of Compliance; file under REG-056/C37.
Record the reporting date and minute reference.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion against all three thresholds is filed and reported.

checklist.step: Scope which roles are engaged in the business of insurance
actions: Map every job family and contractor category against §1033's 'business of insurance' test: agents, adjusters, underwriting, claims, policy servicing, premium handling, executives, and IT/finance roles with transactional authority.
Mark each role IN SCOPE or OUT with a one-line rationale; default borderline roles to IN SCOPE.
Publish the scoping matrix to the Recruiter Talent Acquisition Specialist team and the Producer Compliance Manager.
Revisit the matrix annually and on any new job family.
checklist.done: a published, counsel-owned scoping matrix marks every role IN or OUT with rationale.

checklist.step: Embed the screening gate in the hiring workflow
actions: Configure the Greenhouse pipeline so IN-SCOPE requisitions carry a mandatory 'Background & §1033' stage that blocks offer release until marked clear by the screening team.
Attach the FCRA disclosure and authorization forms and the §1033 attestation to the stage's candidate packet.
Route stage completion to the Compliance Analyst queue, not to the hiring manager.
Test the block by attempting to skip the stage on a dummy requisition and file the result.
checklist.done: no IN-SCOPE offer can release before the screening stage clears, and the block is test-proven.

checklist.step: Collect the candidate's consent and §1033 attestation
actions: Send the FCRA disclosure/authorization and the §1033 attestation through DocuSign; the attestation asks directly whether the person has ever been convicted of a felony involving dishonesty or breach of trust.
Chase unsigned packets at day 3 and day 5; no check may be ordered without the signed authorization.
File the completed envelope against the candidate in the HRIS.
Flag any 'yes' attestation to the Compliance Analyst the same day.
checklist.done: signed consent and attestation are on file before any check is ordered, with 'yes' answers flagged same day.

checklist.step: Order the background check covering the §1033 offense classes
actions: Order the package in LexisNexis Risk: multi-state criminal history, federal district search, SSN trace to widen county coverage, and the sanctions/debarment lists.
Scope the search to at least 7 years and to every county/district surfaced by the trace.
Record the order id and expected return date on the screening case.
For agency principals and contract adjusters, order the same package — engagement channel does not shrink the requirement.
checklist.done: each in-scope person has an ordered package with order id, covering criminal, federal and trace-derived venues.

checklist.step: Adjudicate hits against the dishonesty/breach-of-trust standard
actions: Read each returned record and classify: felony involving dishonesty or breach of trust (fraud, embezzlement, forgery, theft, money laundering) → §1033-prohibited; other records → the ordinary adjudication matrix.
Verify identity match on full name, DOB and SSN trace before treating a record as the candidate's.
Write an adjudication memo per hit with the statute of conviction, date, disposition and classification.
Route every §1033-prohibited classification to Regulatory Counsel within 2 business days; the person may not start in the interim.
checklist.done: every hit carries an identity-verified adjudication memo, with prohibited classifications at counsel inside 2 days.

checklist.step: Run the written-consent path for prohibited persons the business wants to engage
actions: Confirm with the sponsoring executive whether the company will seek consent; absent that, issue the do-not-engage decision.

Prepare the 1033 consent application per the home-state DOI's procedure (most states use the NAIC 1033 consent guidelines): application form, conviction records, rehabilitation evidence, the proposed duties.
File with the state DOI, track the docket and answer information requests within the state's stated windows.
Only a written consent letter naming the person and the permitted activities lifts the bar — file it and restrict duties to its terms.
checklist.done: no prohibited person starts without a filed, granted consent letter, with duties restricted to its scope.

checklist.step: Follow FCRA adverse-action steps for declines
actions: Send the pre-adverse-action notice with the report copy and the CFPB summary of rights, and hold the decision open at least 5 business days for dispute.
Route disputes to LexisNexis Risk for reinvestigation and pause the clock until resolved.
Send the final adverse-action notice with Employment Counsel's sign-off.
File both notices on the case.
checklist.done: every screen-based decline shows the two-notice FCRA sequence with counsel sign-off and dispute handling.

checklist.step: Clear the gate and release the start
actions: Mark the Greenhouse screening stage CLEAR only when the report is returned, all hits adjudicated, and no unresolved §1033 classification stands.
Record the clearance date, adjudicator and evidence links on the screening case.
For agents and adjusters, notify the Producer Licensing Coordinator that the §1033 gate is clear so onboarding may proceed.
Verify HRIS start dates: no in-scope start date may precede its clearance date.
checklist.done: clearance is recorded with adjudicator and date, and no start date precedes it.

checklist.step: Screen existing agency principals at contract and renewal
actions: Require the §1033 attestation and background authorization in every new agency agreement and at each agreement renewal.
Order checks on principals and on any agency staff soliciting under the agreement, tracking them in the agency/producer management system.
Block agency activation in the system until the principal's screen clears.
Record the screen reference on the agency record.
checklist.done: no agency activates or renews without cleared principal screens recorded on the agency record.

checklist.step: Run the annual re-attestation campaign by July 1
actions: Launch the HRIS campaign to all in-scope workers 45 days before the reinsurance year start: re-sign the §1033 attestation including an obligation to disclose new convictions.
Send T-30 and T-14 reminders and escalate non-responders to managers at T-7.
Suspend system access for anyone unattested at July 1 until they complete.
File the campaign completion report.
checklist.done: 100% of in-scope workers re-attested by July 1 or suspended, with the completion report filed.

checklist.step: Handle post-hire conviction disclosures and discoveries
actions: On any disclosure or discovery of a new conviction, open a tracker issue and obtain the court record within 10 business days.
If the conviction is §1033-prohibiting, remove the person from all insurance functions the same day the record confirms, pending the consent decision.
Sweep the person's recent work (claims touched, applications handled) with the owning manager and record the review outcome.
Route the consent-or-separate decision to Regulatory Counsel.
checklist.done: confirmed prohibiting convictions trigger same-day removal, a work sweep and a counsel-owned disposition.

checklist.step: Maintain the screening completion register
actions: Maintain one register row per in-scope person: role, engagement type, screen date, adjudication result, attestation date, consent letter reference where applicable.
Reconcile monthly against HRIS active headcount and the agency/producer roster so nobody active is missing a row.
Mark rows aging past re-attestation as overdue.
File the signed monthly reconciliation.
checklist.done: the register reconciles monthly to active headcount and rosters with no unscreened actives.

checklist.step: Restrict access to screening records
actions: Store reports, memos and attestations in an access-restricted area of the compliance evidence repository limited to the screening team and counsel.
Apply the employment-records retention label and the SRA record-period hold.
Log every access outside the screening team.
Purge per schedule only after both retention clocks expire.
checklist.done: screening records sit behind restricted access with dual retention labels and an access log.

checklist.step: Train screeners and managers annually
actions: Deliver annual training to the screening team on §1033 offense classification and to hiring managers on the no-start-before-clearance rule.
Include the duty to report post-hire convictions in the all-staff compliance module.
Track completion in the learning management system and chase to 100%.
File the rosters.
checklist.done: annual training rosters show 100% completion for screeners and hiring managers.

checklist.step: Report screening performance to compliance leadership
actions: Build the quarterly view: screens completed, average clearance days, open adjudications past 10 days, consent cases and their status, re-attestation completion.
Present to the Head of Compliance with open exceptions and dispositions.
Minute decisions and file the deck.
Escalate any active prohibited-person finding to the Head of Compliance immediately, outside the quarterly cycle.
checklist.done: the quarterly report is presented and filed, with prohibited-person findings escalated immediately.

testing.step: Build the population of in-scope starts and re-attestations
actions: Extract all hires and contractor engagements with start dates in the period from the HRIS, and all agency principals activated from the agency/producer management system.
Classify each against the counsel scoping matrix to derive the in-scope set independently.
Pull the July re-attestation campaign population and completion list.
Reconcile the in-scope set to the screening register and list unmatched actives.
testing.done: the in-scope population is derived from the matrix and reconciled to the register with gaps listed.

testing.step: Reconcile start dates against clearance dates
actions: For every in-scope start in the period, compare the HRIS/agency start date to the register clearance date.
List every start preceding clearance as an automatic exception.
Verify suspended-at-July-1 non-attesters actually lost system access by checking the IAM deprovisioning log.
testing.done: every start post-dates clearance or is excepted, and July suspensions are access-verified.

testing.step: Draw the sample
actions: Take 100% of screens with hits, all consent cases and all post-hire disclosures, plus 25 seeded-random clean screens across employees, adjusters and agency principals.
Confirm the random draw covers all three engagement types so no channel escapes testing.
Record seed, population sizes and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: a reproducible sample with full coverage of hits, consents and disclosures is drawn.

testing.step: Trace sampled screens to source evidence
actions: For each sampled person open the case in the restricted repository: signed FCRA authorization, signed §1033 attestation, LexisNexis Risk report with order id, adjudication memo.
Verify the authorization pre-dates the order and the report pre-dates clearance.
Verify the search scope covered the trace-derived counties and the federal districts.
Treat any missing artifact as a fail, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every sampled case holds the full artifact chain in the right order with adequate search scope.

testing.step: Re-adjudicate the sampled hits
actions: Re-read each hit's court record and independently classify it against the dishonesty/breach-of-trust standard before reading the memo.
Compare classifications; any prohibited conviction adjudicated as ordinary is a critical exception.
Verify identity matching (name, DOB, SSN trace) was documented on each memo.
testing.done: independent re-adjudication matches the memos, with any misclassification raised as critical.

testing.step: Verify every consent case against the state letter
actions: For each consent case, read the state DOI consent letter: named person, granted date, permitted activities.
Confirm the person's actual duties in the HRIS job record fit inside the letter's scope and started only after the grant date.
Confirm declined-or-abandoned cases ended in documented non-engagement.
Capture the letters into the workpaper index, not the workpaper body, given sensitivity.
testing.done: every consent case shows a granted letter covering the actual duties, or documented non-engagement.

testing.step: Test the Greenhouse gate and agency activation block
actions: Attempt to release an offer past the screening stage on a test requisition and confirm the block fires.
Inspect the period's stage audit log for any manual override and trace each override's approver and reason.
Verify a test agency cannot activate in the agency/producer management system without a cleared principal screen.
testing.done: both gates hard-stop in test and every production override carries an approver and reason.

testing.step: Recompute the campaign and adjudication deadlines
actions: Recompute the July 1 re-attestation deadline math on the campaign records and the T-30/T-14 reminder dates.
For sampled adjudications, compute order-to-memo days against the 10-business-day standard and prohibited-routing against the 2-day standard.
List breaches even where the outcome was clean.
testing.done: campaign and adjudication timing recompute inside their standards or are excepted.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise one tracker issue per confirmed exception with person reference (coded, not named, in the tracker), defect and §1033 exposure.
Assign root cause (gate bypass, scope error, memo missing, consent scope drift) and an owner with a remediation date.
Route any active-prohibited-person finding to Regulatory Counsel the same day for removal and disclosure decisions.
Carry open items to the next semi-annual test.
testing.done: every exception is logged pseudonymously with root cause, owner and same-day counsel routing where critical.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the conclusion against the zero-tolerance threshold: effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective.
Have the independent reviewer — who ordered and adjudicated none of the sampled screens — sign the workpaper.
Report to the Head of Compliance and the Chief HR Officer; file the workpaper access-restricted under REG-056/C38.
Record the reporting date and minute reference.
testing.done: a signed, access-restricted workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported.

checklist.step: Pull the internal roster extract at quarter end
actions: Within 5 business days after quarter end, export from the agency/producer management system every agent record active at any point in the quarter: NPN, name, agency, status (VERIFIED/SUSPENDED/TERMINATED), permitted states and status dates.
Freeze the extract with a pull timestamp and row count and store it read-only in the quarter's reconciliation folder.
Include terminated-in-quarter agents so termination propagation can be checked.
Record the extract definition version used.
checklist.done: a timestamped, read-only internal extract with row count covers all agents active in the quarter.

checklist.step: Pull the state-side appointment records
actions: Run a NIPR PDB batch report for the writing company's appointments by state, listing every producer the states show as appointed to the company with appointment dates and statuses.
For states whose appointment data is not fully carried in PDB, pull the state DOI's company appointment list from its public lookup and save the dated capture.
Freeze the combined state-side extract with pull timestamps per source.
Note any state whose data is more than 30 days stale and plan a direct confirmation.
checklist.done: a timestamped state-side extract covers every appointment state from PDB plus direct captures where needed.

checklist.step: Pull the RMA-reported roster
actions: Rebuild the agent roster as reported to RMA from the quarter's accepted weekly eDAS agent-record transmissions.
Use accepted records only — rejected rows never reached RMA and must not flatter the comparison.
Freeze the extract with the covered transmission weeks listed.
Hand it to the Producer Licensing Coordinator with the acceptance-report references.
checklist.done: the RMA-side roster is rebuilt from accepted transmissions with the week list and references attached.

checklist.step: Run the three-way match on NPN + state
actions: In the reconciliation workbook, key all three extracts on NPN + state and match internal ↔ state ↔ RMA.

Categorize every non-match: GHOST (state shows an appointment the roster lacks), MISSING (active roster agent with no state appointment where required), STATUS (terminated internally but still appointed at the state, or vice versa), RMA DRIFT (RMA roster differs from internal).
Compute and record match rates per category and per state.
Lock the matched workbook and open one difference row per non-match.
checklist.done: the workbook shows a categorized difference row for every non-match with per-state match rates.

checklist.step: Investigate MISSING differences first — active agents without required appointments
actions: For each MISSING row, confirm against the state matrix whether that state requires carrier appointment for crop lines.
Where required, run a fresh PDB check; if genuinely unappointed, submit the appointment in NIPR Gateway immediately and record whether any business was written in the exposure window.
Hand any business-written case to the Producer Compliance Manager as an escalated exception with a counsel referral.
Cure or reclassify every MISSING row within 20 business days.
checklist.done: every MISSING row is cured by appointment, reclassified with evidence, or escalated with an exposure sweep.

checklist.step: Clear GHOST appointments off the state records
actions: For each GHOST row, verify the person truly has no active relationship — check terminated records and affiliate writing companies before acting.
Submit the termination in NIPR Gateway for genuine ghosts so the company stops paying renewal fees and carrying appearance-of-authority risk.
Where the ghost stems from a state processing error, raise it with the state DOI and log the contact.
Attach each cure confirmation to the difference row.
checklist.done: every GHOST row is terminated at the state, disputed with the state, or reclassified with evidence.

checklist.step: Fix STATUS mismatches in the lagging system
actions: For terminated-internally-but-appointed-at-state rows, submit the overdue state termination and check the original termination event for a missed statutory window (feeding the C36 breach log).
For appointed-at-state-but-suspended-internally rows, verify the internal suspension is still warranted and document why.
Correct the lagging record and note which system was wrong on the difference row.
Trend which direction lags to target the process fix.
checklist.done: every STATUS row shows the lagging system corrected and any missed window fed to the breach log.

checklist.step: Correct RMA DRIFT by the next weekly cutoff
actions: For each RMA DRIFT row, determine whether the internal roster changed without transmission, a transmission rejected silently, or the M13 mapping dropped a field.
Prepare corrected agent records and transmit them in the next weekly eDAS batch, no later than the transaction cutoff date for that week.
Verify the acceptance report clears the drift and attach it to the difference row.
Where a mapping defect caused systemic drift, open a defect ticket and re-run the affected weeks.
checklist.done: every drift row is corrected through an accepted transmission by the next cutoff, with systemic causes ticketed.

checklist.step: Escalate exposure cases with a written sweep
actions: For any difference revealing business written by an unlicensed or unappointed agent, open a tracker exception with the exposure window and policy list from the Policy Administration Platform.
Refer the state-law consequence and any disclosure duty to Regulatory Counsel.
Track the counsel-decided remedy per policy to completion.
Brief the Head of Compliance on every exposure case at the quarter close.
checklist.done: each exposure case carries a policy-level sweep, a counsel decision and completed remedies.

checklist.step: Close the quarter with a signed reconciliation memo
actions: Write the close-out memo: extract timestamps, match rates, differences by category, cures completed, exceptions escalated and anything rolling forward.
Obtain the Producer Compliance Manager's signature within 20 business days of quarter end.
Obtain Head of Compliance sign-off for any difference rolling into a second quarter.
File the memo with the locked workbook.
checklist.done: a signed close-out memo with match rates and roll-forward approvals is filed within 20 business days.

checklist.step: Feed root causes into the onboarding and termination procedures
actions: Aggregate the quarter's difference root causes (event not entered, NIPR reject unworked, mapping defect, state lag).
Propose procedure or configuration changes to the owning teams with due dates.
Verify last quarter's proposed fixes actually landed by re-checking their difference categories this quarter.
Record the follow-through in the close-out memo.
checklist.done: root causes convert into owned fixes and prior fixes are verified against this quarter's rates.

checklist.step: Confirm terminated agents' books were reassigned
actions: For every terminated-in-quarter agent surfacing in the reconciliation, verify in the Policy Administration Platform that in-force crop policies were reassigned to a verified successor.
List any policy still carrying a terminated agent code as a difference row.
Complete outstanding reassignments before the close-out memo.
Record completion on the workbook.
checklist.done: no in-force policy carries a terminated agent code at quarter close.

checklist.step: Verify appointment fee positions against the cures
actions: Quantify renewal fees paid on GHOST appointments cured this quarter and recover or stop them at the next renewal cycle.
Reconcile new appointment fees from MISSING cures to the NIPR Gateway fee report.
Report the fee impact in the close-out memo.
Flag states with recurring ghost fees to the renewal-cycle owner.
checklist.done: the fee impact of ghosts and cures is quantified and fed into the renewal cycle.

checklist.step: Brief agencies on differences originating with them
actions: Send each agency a list of its agents' differences (unreported terminations, unlicensed states) with required actions and dates.
Collect written confirmations of the corrective actions.
Escalate agencies with repeat differences across two quarters to the Producer Compliance Manager for contract review.
File the correspondence with the quarter's workbook.
checklist.done: agencies confirm corrective actions in writing and repeat offenders are escalated.

checklist.step: Retain the quarter's reconciliation records
actions: Archive the locked workbook, source extracts, difference dispositions, cure confirmations and the signed memo under REG-056/C39/<year>-Q<n>.
Apply the SRA retention label (reinsurance year plus 3 years, extended during any review).
Verify retrievability by quarter, NPN and state.
Log retention completion.
checklist.done: the quarter's records are archived, retention-labelled and retrievable by quarter and NPN.

testing.step: Verify all four quarterly reconciliations ran on schedule
actions: Pull the four quarterly workbooks and close-out memos from the compliance evidence repository.
Check extract pull dates fell within 5 business days of each quarter end and memos were signed within 20 business days.
List any quarter late, skipped or closed without signature as an automatic exception.
testing.done: all four quarters evidence on-schedule extracts and signed closes, or are excepted.

testing.step: Re-perform one quarter's reconciliation end to end
actions: Select one quarter (seeded random) and independently re-run the three-way match from the frozen source extracts on NPN + state.
Compare the independent difference list to the workbook's — undetected differences are exceptions against the reconciliation itself.
Verify the frozen extracts' row counts against the source systems' historical queries to prove the extracts were complete.
testing.done: the re-performed match reproduces the workbook's differences with no undetected non-matches.

testing.step: Draw the disposition sample
actions: Take 100% of escalated exposure cases and MISSING rows across the year, plus 25 seeded-random other difference rows spread over all four quarters and categories.
Confirm the random draw touches every difference category (GHOST, STATUS, RMA DRIFT) at least three times.
Record seed, population sizes and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: a reproducible sample with full coverage of exposure and MISSING rows is drawn.

testing.step: Trace sampled cures to primary evidence
actions: For each sampled cured row, open the attached cure confirmation and verify it in the source: NIPR transaction for appointments/terminations, state DOI contact log for disputes, eDAS acceptance for RMA corrections.
For 5 cures, re-check the current state record in NIPR PDB to confirm the cure held.
Compute disposition days per row against the 20-business-day standard.
Capture the verification results into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled cure verifies at source, holds today for the re-checked 5, and its timing is computed.

testing.step: Re-perform the exposure sweeps
actions: For each exposure case, independently query the Policy Administration Platform for the agent's transactions in the exposure window.
Compare to the swept policy list on the tracker exception; unswept transactions are critical exceptions.
Verify the counsel decision exists and each policy's remedy completed.
testing.done: independent sweeps match the recorded sweeps and every policy shows a completed, counsel-decided remedy.

testing.step: Verify RMA drift corrections reached RMA
actions: For sampled RMA DRIFT rows, trace the correcting eDAS transmission and read its acceptance report.
Confirm the correction week's cutoff was the next available after disposition.
For the ticketed systemic mapping defect (if any), verify the affected weeks were re-run and re-accepted.
testing.done: sampled drift corrections trace to accepted transmissions by the next cutoff, with systemic re-runs verified.

testing.step: Check roll-forward discipline
actions: List every difference that appeared in two consecutive quarterly workbooks.
Verify each carried the Head of Compliance roll-forward sign-off.
Treat any difference surviving two quarters unsigned, or three quarters at all, as an exception.
testing.done: all roll-forwards carry the required sign-off and none survive three quarters.

testing.step: Verify the fee and book-transfer follow-through
actions: Recompute the ghost-fee quantification for one quarter and trace the stop/recovery into the renewal cycle records.
For 5 terminated agents, confirm in the Policy Administration Platform that no in-force policy carried their code at the quarter close.
Flag unstopped ghost fees recurring at the next renewal.
testing.done: fee follow-through and book reassignment verify on the sampled quarter and agents.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise one tracker issue per confirmed exception with quarter, category, NPN/state and defect.
Assign root cause (extract incomplete, match logic gap, cure unverified, sweep short) and an owner with a remediation date.
Route undetected-exposure findings to Regulatory Counsel for disclosure assessment.
Carry open items into the next annual test.
testing.done: every exception is logged with root cause, owner, counsel routing where due and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Score the year against the thresholds (four on-schedule quarters, ≥95% 20-day dispositions, zero surviving unappointed actives) and state a conclusion: effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective.
Have the independent reviewer — who prepared none of the reconciliations — sign the workpaper.
Report to the Producer Compliance Manager and the Head of Compliance; file under REG-056/C39.
Record the reporting date and minute reference.
testing.done: a signed workpaper scoring all thresholds with a stated conclusion is filed and reported.

checklist.step: Maintain the register of SRA-governed conduct areas
actions: Keep a register page in Confluence listing every conduct area the SRA and its appendices govern: agent sales conduct and advertising, controlled business limits, loss adjustment (LASH), eligibility and underwriting (FCIC-18010), NRS products (7 CFR 400.713), conflicts of interest and program integrity (Appendix IV), and records/data handling.
Map each area to its procedure, owner, current version, last review date and citations.
Re-derive the area list each reinsurance year from the reissued SRA rather than rolling it forward blind.
Flag any area with no procedure as an immediate gap exception.
checklist.done: the register maps every SRA conduct area to an owned, versioned, cited procedure with no uncovered areas.

checklist.step: Enforce the required structure on every procedure
actions: Check each procedure against the Procedure Governance Standard: purpose, exact citations (SRA section, CFR part, handbook number), responsible roles, step-by-step instructions, evidence artifacts and the escalation path.
Verify citations against the current e-CFR and the reinsurance year's SRA text, correcting stale section references.
Return non-conforming procedures to their owners with the defect list and a 20-business-day fix window.
Record the structure check on the register row.
checklist.done: every registered procedure conforms to the standard with citations verified against current text.

checklist.step: Run the annual review cycle to finish before July 1
actions: Open a review task per procedure in the workflow/case management tool at T-90 before July 1, assigned to the procedure owner.
Require the owner to diff the procedure against the reissued SRA, the crop year's handbooks and the year's RMA bulletins, and record 'no change' findings explicitly with the sources checked.
Track completion at T-60 and T-30 and escalate laggards to the Head of Compliance at T-30.
Close each task only when the reviewed version is approved and republished.
checklist.done: every procedure shows a completed, source-diffed review with a republished version before July 1.

checklist.step: Obtain the dual approvals on every new or changed procedure
actions: Route each reviewed procedure for two signatures via DocuSign: the business owner for operational accuracy (Chief Claims Officer for loss adjustment, Chief Underwriting Officer for eligibility, Head of Distribution for sales conduct) and the Head of Compliance for regulatory adequacy.
Attach the redline against the prior version to the envelope so signers see what changed.
File the completed envelope with the version in the document management repository.
Reject and rework any procedure a signer declines within 10 business days.
checklist.done: each current version carries both signatures with the redline filed alongside.

checklist.step: Watch RMA bulletins and trigger interim updates within 45 days
actions: Monitor RMA's Manager Bulletins and Product Management Bulletins page (rma.usda.gov ▸ Bulletins) weekly and log each bulletin in the Internal Regulatory System with an impact call per conduct area.
For impacting bulletins, open an interim update task on the affected procedure with a due date 45 days from the bulletin date.
Push urgent operational changes (loss adjustment procedure changes mid-claim-season) to the field by memo immediately, ahead of the formal republication.
Record 'no impact' calls with rationale so the watch is auditable.
checklist.done: every bulletin has a logged impact call and impacting ones drive updates landed within 45 days.

checklist.step: Gate NRS and companion products through 7 CFR 400.713 clearance
actions: Intercept every product proposed for sale in conjunction with an eligible crop insurance contract that FCIC does not reinsure (hail endorsements, wind riders, supplemental bands) at the product-approval gate.
Verify the 7 CFR 400.713 submission to FCIC was made and the waiting/response requirements of 400.714 satisfied before any sale, and file the submission confirmation.
Check with Regulatory Counsel that the product does not shift or increase FCIC's risk — the reinsurance-denial trigger in the SRA.
Log each product's clearance status in the tracker and block launch until CLEARED.
checklist.done: no NRS product sells without a filed 400.713 submission, a counsel risk-shift check and a CLEARED status.

checklist.step: Maintain NRS underwriting information ready for FCIC request
actions: Keep the underwriting files for every NRS product — rates, eligibility rules, loss experience — indexed in the document management repository by product and crop year.
On an FCIC request, assemble and deliver the information within 45 days of the request date, tracked by the countdown alert.
Record the delivery confirmation on the product's tracker entry.
Verify the index quarterly so a request never starts with a search.
checklist.done: NRS underwriting files are indexed and any FCIC request is answered within 45 days with confirmation filed.

checklist.step: Publish procedures to the people who execute them
actions: Publish each approved version to the controlled SharePoint library that field staff, adjusters and agencies actually use, replacing the prior version the same day.
Announce material changes through the field communication channel naming what changed and from when.
Verify agency-facing extracts (sales conduct rules) reach agency principals via the Broker & Agent Portal.
Retire superseded versions from circulation while archiving them.
checklist.done: current versions are the only ones in circulation, with material changes announced and agencies served.

checklist.step: Collect attestations and train on materially changed procedures
actions: For each materially changed procedure, assign the affected population a read-and-attest task or a training module in the learning management system, due within 30 days of publication.
Track completion weekly and chase to 100% through line managers.
Feed loss-adjustment procedure changes into the adjuster crop-year refresher content.
File completion rosters against the procedure version.
checklist.done: every material change shows a 100% attestation or training roster filed against the version.

checklist.step: Check conduct findings against the procedures that should have prevented them
actions: Review quarterly the conduct findings from claims quality reviews, agency audits, complaint investigations and any RMA review against the procedure that governs each area.
Classify each finding: procedure adequate but not followed, or procedure gap.
Open a procedure change task for every gap classification with a 45-day due date.
Report the classification split to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: every conduct finding is classified and each procedure gap drives a dated change task.

checklist.step: Log and cure library exceptions
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any conduct area uncovered, review missed at July 1, bulletin update past 45 days, or NRS product found selling unclear.
Assign root cause (owner vacancy, watch missed the bulletin, gate bypassed) and an owner with a remediation date.
For NRS breaches, stop sales the same day and refer the FCIC disclosure question to Regulatory Counsel.
Track cures weekly until closed.
checklist.done: every library exception is logged with root cause and owner, and NRS breaches stop sales same day.

checklist.step: Obtain remediation sign-off
actions: Review each cured exception against its issue — procedure written, review completed, update landed, NRS cleared or withdrawn.
Obtain the Regulatory Counsel counter-signature on NRS clearance defects and any FCIC disclosure decision.
Sign and date the issue to close it.
Order an interim library health check where exceptions cluster.
checklist.done: no exception closes without the required signatures and disclosure decisions recorded.

checklist.step: Keep version control airtight
actions: Store every approved version as a locked PDF in the document management repository with version number, approval date and signers.
Preserve the full version chain so the procedure in force at any past date is provable — RMA reviews look backwards.
Reconcile the Confluence live pages against the repository versions quarterly.
Apply the SRA retention label to the chain.
checklist.done: the version chain proves what was in force at any date and reconciles to the live library quarterly.

checklist.step: Stand ready for RMA Manual 14 program reviews
actions: Maintain a standing review pack: the register, current versions with approvals, the year's bulletin log with impact calls, and NRS clearance confirmations.
Refresh the pack after the July 1 cycle and after each quarter's exceptions close.
Run an annual dry-run producing the pack inside 5 business days.
Log the dry-run result and fix any retrieval failure.
checklist.done: a refreshed review pack exists and the annual dry-run proves 5-day producibility.

checklist.step: Report library health to governance annually
actions: Build the annual view: coverage rate, review completion before July 1, bulletin-update timeliness, attestation rates, findings-to-gap ratio and NRS clearance status.
Present to the Head of Compliance and the compliance committee before the reinsurance year starts.
Minute decisions on ownership, resourcing and problem areas.
File the deck and minutes with the year's evidence.
checklist.done: the annual health report is presented, minuted and filed before the reinsurance year starts.

testing.step: Rebuild the conduct-area universe from the SRA
actions: Independently derive the list of conduct areas the reinsurance year's SRA, appendices and Manual 14 govern, without reference to the register.
Compare the derived list to the register; any governed area absent from the register is an automatic exception.
Record the derivation sources in the workpaper.
testing.done: the register is proven complete against an independently derived conduct-area universe.

testing.step: Verify every registered procedure's review beat July 1
actions: Pull every review task for the cycle from the workflow/case management tool with completion and republication dates.
Check each procedure's approved version date precedes July 1 and its DocuSign envelope carries both required signatures.
List late reviews, missing signatures and 'no change' findings without recorded sources as exceptions.
testing.done: every procedure shows a dual-signed version republished before July 1 or an exception.

testing.step: Draw the sample
actions: Sample 8 procedures (seeded random, mandatory inclusion of loss adjustment, sales conduct and the NRS clearance procedure).
Take 100% of impacting bulletins and 100% of NRS products sold in the period.
Record seed, population sizes and selection date.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering the mandatory procedures, all impacting bulletins and all NRS products is drawn.

testing.step: Re-verify citations and content currency on sampled procedures
actions: Re-read each sampled procedure's citations against the current e-CFR (7 CFR 400.713–714, 457.8) and the reinsurance year's SRA sections.
Spot-check three operational steps per procedure against the current handbook text (LASH, FCIC-18010) to confirm the steps match today's requirements.
Treat a stale citation or a step contradicting current handbook text as an exception.
testing.done: sampled procedures cite current text and their steps match the current handbooks.

testing.step: Re-perform the bulletin impact calls
actions: Independently read every RMA bulletin logged in the period and form your own impact call before reading the recorded one.
Compare calls; a bulletin marked 'no impact' that actually changed a conduct area is a critical exception.
For impacting bulletins, recompute bulletin date + 45 days and compare to the republication date of the updated procedure.
testing.done: independent impact calls match the log and all updates landed within the recomputed 45-day windows.

testing.step: Trace every NRS product to its 400.713 clearance
actions: Build the sold-product list from the Policy Administration Platform for products written in conjunction with crop contracts and not reinsured by FCIC.
Trace each to a filed 400.713 submission confirmation, the counsel risk-shift check and a CLEARED status pre-dating first sale.
Verify any FCIC information request in the period was answered within 45 days by reading the delivery confirmation.
A sale pre-dating clearance is a reportable breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: every NRS product traces to a pre-sale clearance and FCIC requests were answered within 45 days.

testing.step: Test publication and attestation reach
actions: For each sampled materially changed procedure, confirm the SharePoint library holds only the current version and the superseded version is archived.
Foot the attestation roster in the learning management system to the affected population from HR and roster records.
Interview two field executors per sampled procedure to confirm they work from the current version.
Flag population shortfalls in the roster footing.
testing.done: current-version-only circulation and complete attestation footings are evidenced for sampled changes.

testing.step: Verify the version chain proves what was in force
actions: Pick three past dates and, from the repository version chain, prove which version of each sampled procedure was in force on each date.
Confirm locked PDFs carry version, approval date and signers matching the DocuSign envelopes.
Treat any date the chain cannot answer as an exception.
testing.done: the version chain answers all three point-in-time tests with signer-consistent locked versions.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise one tracker issue per confirmed exception with procedure/product, defect and SRA/CFR impact.
Assign root cause (universe drift, review slippage, watch miss, gate bypass, chain gap) and an owner with a remediation date.
Route NRS breaches to Regulatory Counsel for the FCIC disclosure decision the same day.
Carry open items into the next annual test.
testing.done: every exception is logged with root cause, owner, same-day counsel routing for NRS breaches and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Score the year against the thresholds (100% coverage reviewed before July 1, zero NRS sales without clearance, 45-day bulletin updates) and state a conclusion: effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective.
Have the independent reviewer — who owns and authored none of the tested procedures — sign the workpaper.
Report to the Head of Compliance and the compliance committee; file under REG-056/C40 in the compliance evidence repository.
Record the reporting date and minute reference.
testing.done: a signed workpaper scoring all thresholds with a stated conclusion is filed and reported.
